_comment: The Roadmap page's data. roadmap.html shows it through assets/roadmap.js. Edit this file, not the page, to change what the roadmap says.
Shape: { updated: 'YYYY-MM-DD', latestRelease: 'x.y.z', areas: [area names in filter-chip order], lanes: [lane], upcoming: {...}, releases: [release, newest first] }.
lane: { id: 'done' | 'working' | 'planned', title, note, groups: [group] }. The 'done' lane also takes releasesTitle and releasesNote, and shows the release timeline above its groups.
group: { title, note, id (the anchor, e.g. roadmap.html#rolling-out; optional, defaults to the title as a slug), items: [item] }.

item: { id (anchor, optional), title, text, status, label, area, details: [string | { text, items: [string] }], link (optional): { href, text } }. status picks the badge colour from site.css: released, next, progress, rolling, planned or idea. label is the badge's words. area must be one of 'areas'. Give every item at least one detail: they fill its Details disclosure.

release: { version, date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', title, href (its GitHub release), note (optional line under the title), highlights: [{ text, area }], items (optional: full items, drawn as cards on the timeline instead of a highlights list) }. upcoming: { version, when, note, link } is drawn at the top of the timeline.

Labels: shipped = the release timeline. The newest release's items use status "next" and the label "New in x.y.z"; when the next release comes out, give them status "released" and the label "In x.y.z" (or swap them for a short highlights list). Built but waiting on a part outside Studio, such as the Studio bot = "Rolling out" (rolling); being built = "In progress" or "In progress for x.y.z" (progress); decided, not built = "Planned" (planned); not decided = "Idea" (idea).
Honesty: no invented numbers or dates. Credits are earned only: never bought, never for inviting people, never tied to Discord activity. Discord is the easiest way in, never required.
After editing, refresh the <noscript> copy in roadmap.html with the command at the top of assets/roadmap.js.

lanes.title: Done
lanes.note: Eight releases since the first public one on 22 September 2026. The download is 0.5.0.
lanes.releasesNote: Newest first. Each one links to its release notes on GitHub.

groups.title: New in 0.5
groups.note: In 0.5, the latest release. It took in what was planned for 0.4.5 and 0.4.6.

items.title: The 0.5 layout: one frame for Social and Studio
items.text: A top bar with the Social | Studio switch, a list on the left, an inspector on the right and a status bar, around every page.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: It is Studio’s only layout. The classic tab row, sidebar menus and toolbars are gone, about 2,600 lines of Studio’s own code, and every control they held has a place in the new one.
The rail has four places, Work, Map, Team and Friends, with Search, Settings and Help at its foot. Each place remembers where you were.
Drag the list and the inspector to resize them, or use the keys. In a small window they fold into drawers.
The top bar says where you are; the status bar shows what is working, what waits on you, usage, the machine’s load and the time left on what is playing.
Settings, Search (Ctrl K) and a three-step first run are rebuilt for it.

items.title: Social and Studio: two modes, two moods
items.text: Vibe is now Social, for hanging out with friends and keeping a light eye on your agents. Build is now Studio, for in-depth building, with the social side still there.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Only the names change: your saved mode, settings and links carry over.
Ctrl+M or the switch in the top bar changes mode. Every launch starts in Social unless you turn off Always start in Social in Settings; then Studio opens the mode you last used.

items.title: The Map: your agents’ tree beside your sessions
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: The Command view is now the Map. Your sessions stay in the list beside it, and a small bar over the tree holds Map | Fleet | Pipelines, Running only and View.
details: Pipelines is the Agent brain’s live work. Running only dims everything that isn’t running, and is remembered on this PC.
View holds the five layouts, labels, the camera, and a flat map or a 3D orbit that can spin.
N opens a new task and S opens Search. Fit and zoom sit bottom right, and the colours of the four states bottom left.
Pages that open over the Map show one page at a time, without the tree showing through.

items.title: Today, and one Inbox for everything waiting on you
items.text: Both modes open on Today: your box to build or ask, and a board of what needs you, what runs, what to review and what is done.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Questions, permissions, approvals, reviews and stopped tasks are one list everywhere: the top bar, the status bar, the tabs and Work › Inbox.
Answer from the card, decide later, or open the task.
A Windows notification opens the task it was about, or the Inbox when it told you about several things.
A task that will fix itself, such as a check it tries again, is listed with running work as “Fixing itself”, and reaches the Inbox only if it gives up.
A question shows its choices first, with a small “Answer in my own words” link for anything else.

items.title: Studio mode: your tasks as sessions
items.text: Studio mode lists the project’s tasks like a coding-agent app lists sessions, and each opens as a thread with an inspector beside it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: The thread shows the brief, every run with its steps, notes, questions and answers, and before and after shots.
The inspector has Plan, Changes, Checks, Preview and Agent, plus Worktree for a run in its own worktree.
A box at the foot takes a Note, an Ask or a Change, with pictures and the @ # / picker.

items.title: Team: everything about your agents, in twelve places
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Agents is now Team: Overview, Providers, Seats and models and Permissions, then Rules, Skills, Connectors, Related folders and Workflows, then Health and usage, Models and Inspect.
details: Seats and models opens on who does what in plain words, with one line per job: its model, how hard it thinks and its results on this PC.
Providers starts with “Use one provider for everything” and your subscription logins. Using one subscription for the whole studio now switches every project’s saved team too.
Longer how-to text waits behind a small “i” beside a title: click it, or rest the pointer on it.
Old links, Search and Find a setting land on the place that holds a control now.

items.title: Tabs you add and pin
items.text: Open any page or session in a tab, pin the ones you keep, and Studio keeps the rest tidy.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A preview tab for pages you only glance at, a badge when an agent needs you, at most 8 unpinned tabs (you choose), and Recently closed.
Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+1 to 9. Each project keeps its own tabs; pinned pages follow you.
Every behaviour has its own switch.

items.title: See what changed, and take it back
items.text: After a worker runs, Studio shows the files it changed and lets you accept them or revert a file or the whole attempt.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A private before and after copy of the folder for each attempt, so a revert can be undone.
Studio runs the project’s lint and typecheck after an attempt and shows the result as advice, never as a gate.
When Studio’s own preview is running, it keeps a before and after screenshot.

items.title: Connectors
items.text: Team › Connectors adds, approves, tests and imports MCP servers, and you choose which ones the chat, the helper agents and the builders get.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Studio shows the exact command before anything runs, and finds a server’s tools by itself.
It imports the servers Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI already use, and keeps their tokens encrypted.
Online (Streamable HTTP) servers work too.
The tool calls a model asks for in one turn run side by side, and a server stays open between calls, so a browser it opened is still there for the next click.

items.title: Thinking that steps up when a job gets stuck
items.text: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode start every job with light thinking, and think harder only when a job fails its check.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: After two misses a stronger model takes the job. Max thinking waits for your OK.
Seats and the chat on Claude Code or Codex take a thinking level of their own.
When a harder level keeps working for one kind of job, that kind of job starts there.

A report card in Team › Seats and models says what each model is good and bad at on this PC. A kind of job the usual model keeps failing can try another model for its next five jobs, and keeps it only if it did clearly better.

items.title: Skills any way you want them, and rules for your agents
items.text: Team › Skills keeps the project’s skills with an editor and live checks, and Team › Rules sets what every agent should always do.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Every skill can be always on, picked by the agent when it fits, or used only when called, separately for the chat, Studio’s helper agents and the builders.
A skill that fits is loaded when it’s needed instead of being pasted into every request, and a task that says /skill-name gives its builder that skill.
Skills are written only under the project’s .agents/skills folder.
Studio’s own models can list a project’s folders and search its text when you allow it.

items.title: Answers like you’re five, or the way you pick
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Mefi explains things simply unless you pick another style: Short answers, Teach me, Brainstorm, Poke holes, Expert or plain.
details: A chip beside the permission mode in each message box shows the style and changes it. /eli5, or any other style, in a message uses it once.
A reply shows chips for the skills and tools it used.

items.title: Agents and Studio send only what changed
items.text: When a task changes, Studio sends the window that one card instead of the whole board, and Claude Code and Codex runs show their steps while they work.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: About 5 KB for a change instead of about 690 KB on a 134-card board. Nothing on screen changes.
A Claude Code or Codex run shows its to-do list, the tool it is running and its token use as it goes, as OpenCode runs already did.
Prompts put the parts that stay the same first, so providers that cache them (Zen’s GPT models, OpenRouter’s Claude and Gemini models) can bill them as cache reads.
A coding tool is stopped when Studio stops waiting for its answer, instead of running on for minutes on your subscription.
Each of these has its own off switch.
Still planned: a work journal for each task, and a retry that carries on where the agent left off.

items.title: Studio’s log is kept
items.text: Studio’s log, the assistant’s log and the window’s warnings are saved on this PC and packed into monthly archives that are never deleted.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: They live in the local app-data folder, never in OneDrive.
Trace’s Load older pages back past the last few thousand lines, and Open file shows the folder.
Trace also shows one line per launch with how long each startup step took.

items.title: Size and density, with a live preview
items.text: Make text and information bigger or smaller and see a miniature of the window change before you apply it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Interface scale, text size, three densities and three detail levels.
Ctrl +, Ctrl − and Ctrl 0 change the scale, and it is remembered.

items.title: Chrome: matte black, brushed metal, an iridescent finish
items.text: A new theme and the look new installs open in: matte black panels, silver type, brushed chrome on the main buttons and the side of a switch you are on, and an iridescent finish on the edges and highlights.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Silver, ice blue, lilac and aqua on the selection bars, the open tab, the hairlines and the greeting; silver nodes on the Map; the same palette as this website.
A theme you already picked, Aurora included, stays; every other theme is still there.
The colours that mean something (working, needs you, errors, review) are unchanged.

items.title: Windows tells you when something needs you
items.text: A question, an approval or a failed task that waits while you are away becomes a Windows notification.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: The taskbar icon flashes and shows a count.
Quiet hours, shared with the Discord remote. Finished tasks are off by default.

items.title: Report a problem, and What’s new after an update
items.text: Report a problem builds a zip you can read first, with keys, names and paths taken out. Nothing is uploaded.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: After Studio closes unexpectedly it offers the same report once.
After an update, a short What’s new says what changed.

items.title: Undo for deletes, versions for plans
items.text: A deleted task or idea can be brought back from Recently deleted, and every edit of a plan is kept as a version you can restore.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Search (Ctrl K) starts with what you used last and can add work: type “task …” or “idea …”.

items.title: Pictures on a message, and the @ # / picker
items.text: Paste or drop a screenshot into your message, and type @, # or / to pick a file, a task or a command.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Pictures go to models that can see them; a coding tool is told where the picture is.
Each task can have its own time limit, and its evidence shows its usage.

items.title: Work › Worktrees
items.text: Every git worktree of the project, worst first, with what to do about each: merge into main, remove (keeping a copy of anything at risk) or forget a missing folder.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A run can work in its own worktree; Studio mode marks the tasks that do.
`npm run worktrees` prints the same list for a checkout.

items.title: Other apps: Claude Code, Codex and your scripts can talk to Studio
items.text: Settings › Other apps has a switch, off until you turn it on, that lets apps on this PC see what the agents are doing and what waits on you, message Mefi, hand Studio a task and leave you a note.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Claude Code and Codex connect with one command (an MCP server with eight tools), Cursor, Claude Desktop and VS Code with a JSON block, and scripts and hooks with a command line.
Every task an app files waits for your OK in every permission mode, and approving, answering and settings stay in Studio.
Only this PC can connect, with a key kept in your user folder, and no web page can call it.
Copy setup prompt gives Claude Code, Codex or another AI helper what it needs to walk you through setup.

items.title: Resources: make room for your agents
items.text: Team › Resources lists the other apps on this PC with their CPU and memory, and can hold them back while agents build.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Slow down, Pause, Free memory, Close and End, each undone by Put back or Restore all.
Manual does only what you press. Auto slows heavy apps you aren’t using while agents build, and puts everything back when they finish.
Calls, music, recording, remote access and terminals are left alone unless you say otherwise, and Studio, its agents and Windows are never touched.
Nothing stays paused after Studio closes, even if it crashes. Windows only for now.

items.title: The Studio Daily
items.text: The launch screen is a daily paper: what changed while you were away, before you start.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: It replaces the old launch screen, and stays quiet when nothing changed.

items.title: Use your ChatGPT plan
items.text: Sign in with ChatGPT and route work through the plan you already pay for.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Codex workers run over codex app-server.
GPT-6.1 Sol is the default for the heavy seats.

items.title: A face lift for Models
items.text: Team › Models: the Catalog is one sortable table with four picks, and Performance leads with a leaderboard.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: What the community says about a model, and Studio’s own probes, sit beside it.

items.title: Community model ratings
items.text: A #model-reviews forum in the Discord, run by the bot, with one post per model. Members rate models for each kind of task and share tips.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Ratings feed Studio's model picks from real use: the provider's release notes first, then comments sorted into kinds of task, then tests Studio can run when you ask.
Community evidence only nudges a pick a little.
Studio's model tracker gets a refresh too.

items.title: Sub-agents on the Map
items.text: A session’s sub-agents hang under it on the Map, pop out of their parent, and fly home into it when they’re done.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: The newest three show under each session, with "+n sub-agents" for the rest.
A delegated part flies home into the task that handed it out once it closes.
Your node style's finishing beat plays as work flies home.

items.title: Playlists in the media menu
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Five starting lists of real videos, lists of your own, and a + to save any video.
details: The starting points: Code & math explorers, Visualizers, Focus streams, Shaders & graphics and Simulated worlds.
Make a list from scratch or from Up next, and drag rows to reorder.
Share copies a list as text that reads well in Discord, with a link that plays it on YouTube. Paste that text back and Studio turns it into a playlist.

items.title: A smaller media player with a video feed
items.text: The media menu becomes a mini player with play, pause, back, forward and volume, quick switches for the node tree, and YouTube videos to scroll through.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Click a video to add it to Up next, or drag it into place.
A docked video no longer jitters while the menu scrolls.

items.title: Smooth frames at high tree brightness
items.text: With Tree brightness above 100%, the node tree could slow the whole window down. A fix that brightens each layer once, instead of every shape, is built.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Built on main.

items.title: The setup helper: every agent setting in one place
items.text: One guided menu covers everything that decides what your agents do. Quick setup takes three steps, and Search reaches every section.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Sections: Connect an AI, Team & models, Routing, How work runs, Permissions, Tools & skills, Machine & app, and Look.
It opens first on a new install, and once after you update.
Settings that used to save but do nothing now work.

items.title: A friendlier first run
items.text: With no AI connected, Studio says so and offers Connect an AI instead of "Waiting for you".
items.label: New in 0.5
details: With no coding tool installed, Start agents tells you to install OpenCode, Claude Code or Codex instead of failing five times.
Setup finds the login you already have. A tool that's installed but not signed in no longer counts as connected.
Only one welcome shows at a time.
Builds from Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity are checked by Studio's own checks, instead of always waiting for you to confirm them.

items.title: More than one Claude Code or Codex login
items.text: Add a second login, up to six in all. When one hits its usage limit, work moves to the next one straight away.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Find it under Setup › Connect an AI › More than one login.
Other providers are used only once every login is topped out, and only through fallbacks you already allow.
Each login gets its own row in Usage.

items.title: Studio opens the way you want
items.text: A new Agents when Studio opens setting: Resume what I had, Start agents or Keep agents off.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Start with Windows opens Studio in the tray when you sign in, on the project you had open. A PC you leave working keeps working after an update restart.
Find both in Settings › General › Profile & startup.
Studio no longer jumps to the Map after five quiet minutes. That's now a switch, and it's off by default.
Startup no longer sticks on "Picking up where you left off" when the window opens covered or in the tray.

items.title: In-app updates that finish installing
items.text: Update's install step runs after Studio closes, and the guided sign-in windows for coding tools run their steps instead of closing early.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: In 0.4.4 and earlier, Update can download and check a new release, but its install step may not run, so moving from 0.4.4 to 0.5 is by hand, once.
In 0.4.4, the guided install and sign-in windows can close before they run. Sign in from a terminal, then use Check connection.
The portable executable carries Studio’s name, version and icon.

items.title: Agents say why they're not working
items.text: Today, the Map, a task’s page and the chat all give one answer about what is holding work back, with the one control that clears it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: It names a pause, a cooldown, tasks waiting for your OK and the permission mode holding them, the free model's one-at-a-time limit, and more.
Approving a task before its references finish gathering no longer drops the approval.
Permission modes keep their meaning when an older switch or a brain map changes them.
The answer follows a project switch straight away.

items.title: Watch Mefi think and your team work
items.text: In Social mode, Suggest a next step and Build it show live progress instead of one still sentence.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: See the stage reached, the files read or steps planned, which model is thinking, and a clock against how long it usually takes on your PC.
A split request draws its steps as a track to the final check.
Adding one suggestion to your draft no longer locks the others.

items.title: Build on your app with MEFI
items.text: Social mode offers Modify, Experiment, Fix and Improve, with briefs based on your project map.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Suggestions can go into a draft, or be saved as ideas without starting work.
The map shows which systems change together.
A separate Ideas tree groups ideas and tasks by system and progress.

items.title: Plans, one step at a time
items.text: Plans shows one step at a time, with a button to the step that's waiting on you and a progress track.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: The interview reads as a chat, and Mefi asks the next question on its own. You can switch that off.
Plans opens without waiting for the folder scan, and gets your project ready in the background.
A quick model answers first. If its reply misses, the deeper model gets one go, and Think harder goes straight to it.
A new idea needs no name and has starters, and Where this lives pins a plan to an area of the Project map.

items.title: A calmer Task board
items.text: The board opens on its tools, cards are tighter, and a click anywhere on a card opens its task.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Add, then search with the state picker beside it, then the All, Open, Review and Done chips in one row.
Cards slide up into free space instead of waiting below the tallest card in their row.
← All cards closes a task at any width, and the status box sits at the top of Details.

items.title: Habits for each agent
items.text: Short rules an agent follows, such as explain changes, test, take small steps and keep a to-do list.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Each habit can be off, brief or full.
You see what an agent's habits add to every prompt, in tokens.
Find them in Team › Seats and models, on each job’s card under More settings.

items.title: A cleaner Needs you list
items.text: An ask you answered leaves the list straight away.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Old asks, and asks about cards that left the board while Studio was closed, are cleared when the project loads.

items.title: "What changed while I was away?" without an AI
items.text: The chat answers from Studio's report of work done outside it, even with no model connected.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: It says a card "may already be done" when it only matched on file names and commit subjects.

items.title: Configuration: every setting in one tree
items.text: Ctrl Shift , opens every Studio setting in one searchable tree. Picking a setting opens its real control.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: It adds an Interface scale, from 70% to 150%.
It's also in Settings, as All settings in one place.
It also indexes every setup-helper section and pins Walk me through setup. Pick a section to open its real controls.

items.title: Menus that ask the same way and speak plainly
items.text: Every action that can't be undone now asks the same way: the first press asks, the second acts.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Errors read as sentences.
Pages leave out values that were never recorded, instead of printing "undefined" or "Invalid Date".
Menus open, close and reorder smoothly. Reduced motion turns that off.
M+ opens Projects on the project you're in.

items.title: Typing goes into the open menu's box
items.text: When a menu with a text box is open, what you type lands in that box instead of setting off single-letter shortcuts.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Clicking out of the menu gives the keys back.

items.title: A media player you can always reach
items.text: Floating players get a move handle and Settings, minimize and close buttons. A minimized player leaves a restore bar.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Websites get the full panel width.
The player takes keyboard focus only when you minimize it yourself.

items.title: Every node style finishes in its own way
items.text: In the Agent brain, a step whose work came back, and the lead taking its agent in, play your node style's own finishing beat.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Classic orbs' ring bursts, Soft glass ripples like a drop on water, Minimal draws a check, Halo slips its ring over the lead, Crystal glints across its facets, Singularity's disc flares, Prism shatters and fuses back, and Sigil's rune writes itself shut.
A failed check finishes in amber. With reduced motion on, the Agent brain plays no beats.
The Agent brain's pipeline list no longer cuts long titles off, and the Playbook shelf keeps its books in tight rows.

items.title: Your companion as a pet
items.text: The companion menu has six bubbles, one job each: Talk, What I'm doing, Needs you, Suggest work, Friends and Personality.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Pet it, and it remembers your days together.
Personality sets how it acts: Straight work, Balanced, or Friendly & expressive.
Practice playdates with Pip, a buddy that stays on your PC. Playdates with friends are part of Friends in 0.5.

items.title: Share between your PCs
items.text: A private GitHub vault, sealed with a key only your paired PCs hold, carries what you choose between your own PCs.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Model results, learned decisions, team setups, brains, recipes, memory notes, preferences, and open tasks and ideas.
Keys and setup can travel too, but only after a typed confirmation.
Each PC's line in Friends › Your PCs says what its agents are working on, what waits for you there and what finished today.

items.title: Share with friends
items.text: Save one brain, recipe, team setup, set of model results, memory note or preferences as a .mefishare file. It's scrubbed and previewed before you save it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A file you receive is reviewed before it can reach your library, and a risky one is kept out.
A friend's file can never change your permissions.

items.title: Set up a new PC and keep every PC current
items.text: Set up this PC is a checklist for Git, the GitHub CLI, Node.js, a GitHub sign-in and the project's packages, with a button for each gap.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Get a project from GitHub clones one of your repositories.
Keep this PC up to date checks GitHub once a minute, and brings in other PCs' work when nothing on this PC is in the way.
Sync this PC now runs the project's checks before it pushes.
Closing Studio asks first when this PC holds work no other PC has.

items.title: Lighter while minimized
items.text: A window in the tray or minimized keeps only the newest board and machine updates, and catches up when you open it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Bursts of status updates are merged into one.
A closed Explorer no longer repaints on every update.

items.title: The Fleet page: your team at a glance
items.text: Fleet, beside the Map (Map | Fleet | Pipelines), shows the open project’s seats in Lead, Build, Check and Keep pods, with the wires between them.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Graph, Table, Recent, Tree and Health views show the team, handoffs, checks and what needs a look.
Each seat opens an inspector with its current work, earlier runs, Open task, a way to its node on the Map and a two-press Stop this run.
It folds its columns to the room it has, so Fit shows the whole team in a narrow window too.
Agent lanes, missions and fleets from other PCs belong to the later Fleet work.

items.title: Sync catches a merge that loses work
items.text: Before pushing, Sync checks whether a merge silently kept one branch’s files and dropped another PC’s changes.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A loss of 200 or more lines stops the push and names the merge and files that need a look.
Friends › Your PCs also reports recent suspicious merges.
The report names the files to inspect before you try to sync again.

items.title: Tidier Ideas cards alongside Tasks
items.text: Ideas gets compact cards with a clear title, a short excerpt and its status. Short cards slide up into free space, as on the Task board.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: The layout adapts when the window changes size, and keeps one column in narrow spaces.
Source and date appear only when recorded, and selecting a card keeps the existing idea detail and actions.
Providers, Plans, Social mode and the Project map’s wider card cleanup stay planned for after 0.5.

groups.title: Friends in 0.5
groups.note: In 0.5, the latest release. Friends runs on the Mefi Studio relay, a free service on Cloudflare that is built into Studio: there is no hub to set up, and no PC has to stay on.

items.title: Friends with no setup
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Rooms, room chat, Listen together, companions in the Playground and cowork file claims all run through the Mefi Studio relay. You no longer enter a hub address.
details: The relay keeps no chat. Your Studio keeps its own encrypted copy of each room’s messages for a week, and fills in what you missed from other members’ copies.
The relay signs every message, so a copy can’t be altered.
Its code is public, in Studio’s repository.

items.title: Friends, a place of its own
items.text: The rail’s Friends opens one roomy page: The Lobby, Rooms, Your PCs, Playground, the Project hub and Events, in the list beside it.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Each place says in one line what it is for, and each can be a tab.
Search and the companion’s Friends bubble open the page at the right place.
Your PCs sums up a long report in a few lines, with Show all for the whole list.

items.title: The Lobby, and rooms like a chat app
items.text: Friends opens on The Lobby: who is online and in which room, the week’s top project, the rooms open now, what was shared this week and who moved up a rank.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Everyone signed in is in the Lobby room, so there is always someone to say hi to.
An open room fills the page: who is here, Listen together, the conversation and one message box. Enter sends, and Shift+Enter starts a new line.
Every room has a short invite code. Copy invite, and a friend types it into Join with a code to come straight in.
Who’s online lists who is in Studio right now, with Invite to a room. Untick Show me as online to hide.
Once you sign in, Studio connects by itself a few seconds after it opens.

items.title: Friends › Rooms
items.text: Browse rooms, ask to join with a note, accept invites, let people in and chat with @names, all inside Studio.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Room owners can invite people by name, make a new invite code, and lock or close their rooms.
A hangout room holds up to 25 people, and a cowork room up to 10.
Anyone a week in the Void Engine server can make an unlisted room. Showing a room in the public list takes the Flame rank.
Rooms use a linked Discord account to know who you are.
Moderators see a message only when someone reports it.

items.title: Listen together
items.text: Play a link for a room, and everyone who picks Listen along joins at the same point.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Whoever put it on, or the room's owner, can pause, restart or stop it.
Share what I'm playing, off by default, lets the bot's /nowplaying show your current link or station once the Studio bot is linked to the relay. It never shows a file's name.
Studio's side has been in the app since 0.4.0.

items.title: Playdates with friends
items.text: Companions on different PCs meet in a room for short playdates, in Friends › Playground.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Nothing about you or your work is shared until you allow it. When a friend's companion shares more, Studio asks whether to share the same back.
What was sent lists everything that left your PC.
Practice with Pip works on your own PC, without signing in.

items.title: Agents on several PCs never edit the same file
items.text: Link a cowork room to a project, and Studio claims the files a builder will edit before it starts. Every PC hears about it within a second.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: A task whose files another PC holds waits and picks other work.
Without a linked room, nothing waits.

items.title: My PCs: your PCs work as one
items.text: Friends › Your PCs lists every PC you sign in to Friends on, live: its CPU, free memory, battery and running tasks, and why it isn’t taking work.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Pair each PC once by checking the same six numbers on both screens. Only paired PCs can send each other work.
Send work here starts a task on another PC, or moves a ready card to it.
When a PC stays busy or short of memory, or a laptop’s battery reaches 20%, its ready cards move to a paired PC with a free slot and the same project open. A card is moved, never copied.
At 10% a laptop saves its progress, parks its changes as a branch another PC can pick up, and waits for Continue.
A friend can lend you their PC: your tasks there wait for their OK unless they choose otherwise.

items.title: Link your Discord account
items.text: Link Discord in Friends asks Discord once, in your browser, and connects by itself. Rooms, The Lobby and the Project hub need it; the rest of Studio never does.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Studio reads only who you are and your membership in the Void Engine server: never your messages, your email or other servers.
If your account isn’t in the Void Engine server yet, it offers Join the Discord and checks again.
No Discord roles are needed: ranks come from credits, and moderators are named accounts.

items.title: The Project hub: share what you make
items.text: Share a project as a card (a public link, a title and a line about it, never a file) and play what friends make. A star map draws every shared project, and New, Top and Mine list them.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Sharing is free, and earns nothing by itself.
Report someone else’s project if it’s spam, a broken link, not safe to open, or someone else’s work.
The Discord’s /showcase and the Made with Studio wall on this site are still there too.

items.title: Credits and ranks, earned by playing
items.text: When you play someone else’s project for two minutes, you both earn credits: 5 for the maker and 2 for you. A star earns the maker 3.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Credits are earned only: never bought, never for inviting people, never for being active in the Discord.
Ranks run Spark, Ember, Flame, Comet, Star, Nova and Void. Your balance is yours alone; others see your rank.

The relay works credits out, never your Studio, and they hold up against second accounts and trading: credits start once a Discord account is 30 days old and a week in the Void Engine server, a play pays once a day per player, and one person can make another earn at most 15 credits a week.

items.title: Friends › Events: a weekly Build Jam and co-work hours
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: A Build Jam every week with a theme, co-work hours three times a day, and credits for building together.
details: The Build Jam opens on Monday with a theme and shows next week’s. Enter one of your shared projects until Saturday, then play the others and vote for up to three until Monday, when the results are paid.
A vote counts only for an entry you played for two minutes, and votes stay hidden until the results.
Three times a day a co-work hour opens a room: join it, keep Studio open and work on anything, and everyone who stays with others earns 4 credits.
Building together in your own co-work room with a friend earns you both 4 credits a day.
Credits come from making and playing things together, never from inviting people. To bring a friend, send them your room’s join code.
Prizes and co-work rewards share a daily community pot that grows with the number of people active that week, so credits keep their worth as the community grows.
Studio shows the jam’s times in your own time zone.

items.title: Feature your project with credits
items.text: Spend 100 credits to put a project at the top of the Project hub for a day.
items.label: New in 0.5
details: Featuring is once a week.
Nobody can buy a better spot: credits are earned only.

items.title: Moderation and reports
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Report a message or a project, and moderators review it in Friends › Moderation, a place only they see.
details: It shows who looks like they are farming credits, the open reports, and a lookup by name.
A moderator can take farmed credits back, suspend someone for a day or a week, or take a project off the hub.
A reported message reaches moderators only when its relay signature checks out, so a report can’t be faked.

items.title: Pop-ups from friends, and Building now
items.label: New in 0.5
items.text: Studio says when someone you share a room with opens Studio, invites you, asks to join your room, or plays or stars your project.
details: Several at once are one pop-up, and the same friend shows at most every 30 minutes. Nobody is announced while they hide from Who’s online.
Pop-ups from friends, at the foot of The Lobby, turns them off.
Share what I’m building, off until you turn it on, shows friends your open project’s name with a small live tree: a lit leaf for each task running. Never task titles or files.

groups.title: In the community
groups.note: The Studio bot in the Void Engine Discord runs on the owner's PC, so it can be offline now and then.

items.title: Show your work with /showcase
items.text: Post a project with a title, a link and a description. The bot adds a short blurb and tags, and pings nobody.
items.label: In the Discord
details: You can thank someone who helped you.
You choose whether your post may be featured.

items.title: Cowork sessions
items.text: /cowork start opens a temporary voice channel and a thread, so you can work side by side.
items.label: In the Discord
details: Both go away 5 minutes after the voice channel empties.

items.title: Help, roles and privacy
items.text: /ask answers questions from the Studio wiki, and in a help thread the asker can mark the reply that solved it.
items.label: In the Discord
details: Roles come from taking part. Builder, Helper and Mentor need a moderator's OK, and Spotlight marks the project of the week.
Roles never come from inviting people or from message counts.
/me shows you your streak and roles, privately. There is no public leaderboard.
/privacy shows what the bot keeps, and /forget-me deletes your records.
Each new Studio release is announced once in the server.

items.title: The Made with Studio wall
items.text: Projects people built with Studio, on this site's Community page. Add yours with a pull request.
items.label: On this site
details: Every entry is a pull request, so it's looked over before it appears.
With your OK, a project shared in the Discord can go on the wall too.

lanes.title: Being worked on
lanes.note: Being built right now, or built and waiting to switch on.

groups.title: Moving to Rust
groups.note: Studio is moving from Electron to Rust (Tauri 2) in three stages, started on 3 October 2026. The app keeps working at every step: the same screens, settings and saved keys. The download is still the Electron build, and the switch has no date.

items.title: Stage 1: the Rust host
items.text: Rust runs the window, the tray, dialogs, notifications, saved keys and the page’s bridge. The engine runs beside it, unchanged.
items.label: Built on main
details: A source checkout runs on it with `npm run host`; a portable build can ship on it (`npm run package:host`).
The updater in this version can install either kind of build and roll back from either.
The interface stays HTML and JavaScript, in WebView2.

items.title: Stage 2: the engine moves into Rust
items.text: The engine’s parts move into Rust one by one, each giving the same answers as the JavaScript it replaces.
items.label: In progress
details: Moved so far: the OpenCode session store, multi-PC sync and the Worktrees page, the @ picker’s file search, the Git chip, the Skills page’s files, a message’s pictures, before and after pictures and Revert, and settings and saved keys.
A test runs both engines on every moved part and holds them equal.
The OpenCode usage ledger’s repeat reads are about nine times faster in Rust.
Next come the engine’s logic, then the services that start the builders.

items.title: Stage 3: one Rust program
items.text: A release carries only the Rust host: no Node runtime and no sidecar.
items.label: Planned
details: The first update from an Electron build to it needs a bridge release, which is part of this stage.

items.title: A faster launch
items.text: Studio opens sooner, without the blank fade.
items.label: In progress for 0.5.x
details: Built so far: timing marks for every startup step, a settings cache, and a compile cache for Studio’s own code.
Still to do: a shorter launch gate, and fewer calls at startup.

groups.title: In progress
groups.note: Started, not finished. On branches or in other repositories, not on main yet.

items.title: New things for the Studio bot
items.text: A welcome for newcomers, celebrations you can switch off, /trivia, a prompt of the day and /help.
items.label: In progress
details: A digest in the server when new AI models come out, marking the ones Studio already offers.
@mention the bot to chat with it.
Memory is opt-in: it keeps notes about you only with your OK, and /forget-me wipes them.
It will ping everyone only for new Studio releases.
Built on a branch of the bot. Not live yet.

groups.title: Rolling out
groups.note: Studio’s side is in 0.5. This switches on once the Studio bot’s side is live.

items.title: Reach this PC from Discord
items.text: Friends › Your PCs › Reach this PC from Discord lets you DM the bot in the Void Engine Discord to check on this PC and talk to Mefi there.
items.label: Rolling out
details: See what needs you and what's being made, pause or resume the agents, or just message Mefi.
Work you start from Discord waits for your OK, and approving from Discord needs a PIN you set in Studio.
Only your own Discord account gets answers, and no port opens on your PC.
Studio’s side is in 0.5, and the relay carries it. It works once the Studio bot is linked to the relay; the bot’s side is still being built.

lanes.title: Planned
lanes.note: Decided but not built yet, then the bigger plans and ideas. Nothing here has a date, and details can change.

groups.title: Planned
groups.note: Decided. No version or date yet.

items.title: Linux
items.text: A Linux build of Studio. No date yet.
items.label: Planned
details: Studio's checks and tests already run on Linux for every change to main, and the app opens in a test window there.

items.title: A bridge to your creative tools
items.text: Studio connects to Blender, Godot and Unity through MCP.
items.label: Planned
details: Setups that need no AI at all, like a player beside a project that Studio watches.
Coding agents that build the support for a new tool.
AI stays optional, and no single service is required.
Connectors, in 0.5, can already add an MCP server you have for one of these tools.

items.title: Fleet lanes, missions and other PCs
items.text: The next Fleet phases add a lane per agent, progress measured from verified work, and fleets from your other PCs and friends.
items.label: Planned
details: The first Fleet page is in 0.5, beside the Map. These larger phases come after it.
Lanes you can pause, with a budget; missions with intent, evidence and task progress.
Your other PCs and friends’ fleets follow the sharing level you choose.

items.title: More for Friends: same Wi-Fi, shared trees and a fair video queue
items.label: Planned
items.text: The parts of Friends 2.0 that aren’t built yet.
details: Studios on the same Wi-Fi find each other on their own, after you confirm a matching code once.
Project rooms, with friends’ cursors on a shared tree.
Chat with the Discord bot and see its cards in Studio.

items: Whoever has been in the room longest controls the player.
A newcomer gets one free Play next, then waits 24 hours for another.
Each person's videos play in boxes of three, taking turns.
New members can add videos up to 8 minutes long.
No playlists in the lobby. In a private room, a playlist expands into the queue.
Every queued item shows who asked for it, how long it is and what kind of media it is.

details: Guest passes may come later.

items.title: Signed Windows builds
items.text: Studio’s Windows build will be signed through the SignPath Foundation’s free programme for open-source projects, so Windows stops warning about it.
items.label: Planned
details: The release workflow for it is written and tested. Signing starts once SignPath accepts the project.
Until then, SmartScreen may ask first: choose More info, then Run anyway.

groups.title: After 0.5
groups.note: Decided for the releases after 0.5. No dates yet.

items.title: Three pieces of the 0.5 design
items.label: Planned for 0.5.x
items.text: A live Preview tab inside Studio, the pinned tree strip as a panel, and Drafts in the session list.
details: In the 0.5 design, not built yet. They come in 0.5.x.
Today the inspector’s Preview has the project’s preview controls and Before and After.

items.title: Related folders
items.text: Let a project read from folders beside it, such as a shared library or a design folder.
items.label: Planned for 0.5.x
details: Read-only, and only the folders you name.
Team › Related folders is already there, and says plainly that Studio can’t add them yet.

items.title: Start a new app from a template
items.text: Pick a starting point when you start a new app, instead of an empty folder.
items.label: Planned for 0.5.x
details: New app already makes a folder, starts Git and sends your description as the first request.

items.title: Saved map views
items.text: Keep the way you arranged a map and come back to it.
items.label: Planned for 0.5.x
details: For the project map and Brain maps.

items.title: The tidy-card layout on the remaining menus
items.text: Extend the compact cards and cleanup to Team › Providers, Plans, Social mode and the Project map.
items.label: Planned
details: Task and Ideas cards are in 0.5. This wider rollout comes later.
The card-layout helper is now shared, so later pages can use the same behavior.

items.title: Cowork rooms with GitHub access
items.text: A room can give its members access to a project on GitHub, and their agents coordinate so they don't collide.
items.label: Planned
details: The file claims that keep agents apart are in 0.5 (see Friends in 0.5).

items.title: Shared agent capacity
items.text: Members can offer their coding-agent capacity to a room, under a shared cap.
items.label: Planned
details: Subscription logins are never shared.

groups.title: The community plan
groups.note: The owner’s plan for sharing in Studio. Sharing projects, credits and featuring are in 0.5 (see Friends in 0.5); these parts are still open. Credits will only ever be earned: never bought, never given for inviting people, and never tied to Discord activity.

items.title: Cosmetics and creator styles
items.text: Spend credits on cosmetics, and offer styles you made to other people.
items.label: Planned
details: Every theme and node style in Studio is free today, the Void collection included.

items.title: Shared mixes and most played
items.text: Share your music mixes, and see which ones are played the most.
items.label: Planned
details: Most-played lists count only people who turn on "share music taste" in Friends or their profile.
Share what I'm playing, which feeds the bot's /nowplaying, is a first step. It's off by default.
Playlists in 0.5 can already be shared as text, with a link that plays them on YouTube.

items.title: "Hey Studio" voice
items.text: An optional wake phrase or push-to-talk key opens a listening popup. You check the text before it's sent.
items.label: Idea
details: It would use a speech service you choose, and could answer out loud if you want.
Voice isn't built. Today the microphone only moves the node tree to sound.

items.title: Run as many agents as your PC has room for
items.label: Idea
items.text: Studio would start as many coding agents as free memory allows, reuse agent programs instead of starting one for every task, and show that on screen.
details: Measurements show Studio’s own window and engine idle near 0% CPU, while each coding agent program holds 0.2 to 0.7 GB of memory.
Proposed on 5 October 2026, and waiting for a decision. It would come before more of the engine moves to Rust.

upcoming.note: Next up: 0.5.x, with Related folders, starting a new app from a template, saved map views and the pieces of the 0.5 design still to build. Studio is also moving to Rust, in stages.

releases.title: One layout for Social and Studio, Friends with no setup, and changes you can take back
releases.note: It took in what was planned for 0.4.5 and 0.4.6. On 0.4.4, update by hand once: 0.4.4 can’t install 0.5 by itself.

highlights.text: One layout: Vibe and Build are now Social and Studio, the Command view is the Map and Agents is Team, with tabs you pin, one Inbox and a status bar around every page.
Friends with no setup, on a relay built into Studio: The Lobby, rooms that read like a chat app, the Project hub with credits and ranks, and a weekly Build Jam.
See the files a worker changed, then accept them or revert a file or the whole attempt.
Team › Connectors for MCP servers, skills any way you want them, answer styles, and thinking that steps up only when a job gets stuck.
A three-step first run, the setup helper, more than one Claude Code or Codex login, and your ChatGPT plan.

Windows notifications, Report a problem, What’s new after an update, and in-app updates that finish installing. Other apps lets Claude Code, Codex and your scripts talk to Studio, and Team › Resources makes room for your agents.
My PCs: your PCs share the work, and a laptop low on battery hands its tasks to another.
Chrome, the new default look, Size and density with a live preview, and Playlists in the media menu.

releases.title: One subscription for everything, no work built twice, and every look for free

highlights.text: Start here can set up Codex, Claude Code, Grok or Antigravity, and Use for the whole studio then sends chat, mapping, planning, agents and coding through that one subscription. In 0.4.4 its install and sign-in windows may close too soon: sign in from a terminal, then use Check connection.

Build it in Vibe decides whether a request is one task or two to six steps, and a Plan in flight card follows the steps. New app makes a project folder, starts Git and sends your description as the first request.
When you reopen a project, Studio reports the commits, edits and coding sessions made while it was closed, and checks queued cards against that work so finished work isn't built again.
Four permission modes: Always ask, Accept per task, Auto and Elevated only. Automatic decisions come with a Why and an Undo, and Mefi learns from your answers.
Every theme and node style is free, the Void collection included.
Friends › Your PCs shows whether this PC matches the project on GitHub, and Sync this PC pulls and pushes without force.
Trace shows Studio's logs as channels in one viewer.

releases.title: A media queue, live tree controls and tools for each agent

highlights.text: An Up next queue for copied links and YouTube results, with Play, Queue next and a built-in YouTube explorer. It moves on to the next item by itself.
The node tree can move with the music or a video, in ring, wave or spiral shapes, with controls for size, spacing and position.
Brightness sliders for the nodes, the wires and the video, transparency sliders for the tree and the video, and optional node outlines.
Drop text and code files into Home, Vibe and Plans. Planning reads fresh project excerpts and any files you name.
Each agent can have its own web search, project read permission and allowed MCP tools.

releases.title: Vibe mode and remastered node styles

highlights.text: Vibe mode is one focused workspace for conversation, new tasks, live work and decisions. The full Build workspace is one switch away.
Answer agents' decisions in a drawer inside Vibe. It shows the question and the task it blocks.
Vibe shows what is stopping the agents and offers the fix in place: Start agents, Resume or Connect an AI.
All eight node styles were remastered, each with its own shapes, motion, wires and finish effects.
Plans can be archived and restored.

releases.title: The Agent Brain: watch your agents work and keep what worked

highlights.text: The Agent brain view (key J) shows a task's pipeline from the top down. Sub-agents go out and report back up the tree.
The Playbook files each finished pipeline as a recipe, so the next task of the same kind starts from what worked.
A project map built from your git history and your agents' work, with Work on this region.
A companion lives in the menu. It greets you with what happened while you were away and keeps one list of what needs you.
The Links player plays YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud and Vimeo links, and Home became glass over the live node tree.

releases.title: A regrouped menu, run history and a safer app

highlights.text: The menu was regrouped into Home, Work, Live, Models and Settings, with Search Studio on Ctrl K.
Duplicate cards and repeating work now reach you as one question instead of looping.
Each task shows its run history: who ran it, how it ended and what it changed.
A Usage popover with a card for every provider's plan.
Child processes no longer see Studio's keys, and the web preview only answers on your own PC.
Studio's side of the Discord link, through Discord's own login. It switches on once the link app goes live.

releases.title: One navigation rail, a real Brain maps editor and ad-free radio

highlights.text: One rail down the left edge replaced three separate menus.
Brain maps became a node editor you can pan and zoom, for changing how the agent pipeline decides things.
Ad-free radio from listener-funded stations at SomaFM and Radio Paradise. When a stream stalls, a backup crossfades in.
Planning and reading can each use their own AI provider, and OpenCode Zen became a route.
A loop guard holds cards that keep failing, and says how to release them.
A portable Windows download on GitHub Releases, and an update check that verifies each release's SHA-256.
Brain maps: the agent pipeline as an editable graph. Build with AI drafts one from a sentence.
A seven-stop Start here walkthrough with a Walk with me coach.
Command view's live node tree. Finished work waits in a verification stage, with evidence, before it counts as done.
Routing across many providers: z.ai, OpenCode Go, the Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity command-line tools, LM Studio and custom endpoints.
